item.title: Incarico post-doc: Pica Code IPD-2026-067 - “Stage diplomacy. Reassessing Italy’s performing arts within the context of international relations” (Acronimo “STACY”) (Univ. MODENA e R. E.)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 13:00
Institution: Univ. MODENA e R. E., Modena
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/PEMM-01 Arti performative, musicali, cinematografiche e mediali

The research assignments primarily entail conducting archival research in Italy and abroad to locate sources (e.g., administrative, financial, and epistolary records) that document the relationship between Italian foreign policy, institutions, and the performing arts (drama, opera, and so-called "minor" genres) from the second half of the 19th century to the present, including the analysis of funding and theatrical consumption. Collaboration in teaching and third-mission activities is to be carried out within the scope of the academic discipline field SSD PEMM-01/A.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Postdoctoral assignment - Ancient and Modern Cultures and Languages of Africa and Western Cental Asia (Univ. VENEZIA)
item.description:

Institution: Univ. VENEZIA, Venezia - Venice
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/STAA-01 Culture e lingue antiche e moderne dell'africa e dell'asia occidentale e centrale

This project proposes an exploration of the conceptions of the water cycle and the environment preserved in Arabic sources composed from the twelfth century onwards, during the period commonly defined as post-classical. Although hydraulic engineering in the Arab-Islamic context has been the subject of numerous studies, a history of hydrological thought remains to be written for the centuries following the twelfth. Here, hydrological thought is understood both as systemic reflection on water within the global environment (hydrological cycle, water balance) and as the study of specific phenomena related to it, such as precipitation and its relationship with orography, groundwater and karst…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Persistences and Metamorphoses. Narrative Forms and the History of Ideas in Comparative Literature. (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:

Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/COMP-01 Comparatistica e teoria della letteratura

This post-doctoral position falls within the fields of comparative literature and the history of ideas, with a focus on Italian, English, and French literatures. item.description:

Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/ARTE-01 Storia dell'arte

The Marisa Volpi archive: reorganization, description, electronic indexing, and initiation of digitization. Specifically, the assignment pursues the following general objective: To establish a permanent digital documentary infrastructure for the collection of the critic, art historian, and writer Marisa Volpi (1928–2015)—donated to the SARAS Department by her heirs—thereby ensuring its preservation and accessibility, and making it available to the scholarly community for research into Italian and international art from the post-World War II period and the concurrent network of intellectual, critical, and institutional relationships.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Gathering the Landscape. Building a Corpus of Representations of Italy in Spanish Texts of the Sixteenth and Seventeenth Centuries (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 12:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/SPAN-01 Lingue, letterature e culture spagnola e ispano-americane

The research will focus on building SAIL’s textual corpus for its first historical phase, through a survey of Spanish texts representing the Italian landscape between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries and spanning different textual genres (memoirs, autobiographies, correspondence, as well as pre-periodical), based on archival research in Spanish and Italian institutions. The analysis of selected case studies will also contribute to an initial mapping of the places represented, recurring motifs, and representational techniques, with a view to defining the expressive ‘code’ of landscape representation.
